title: Grilled Beef Kebabs with Peppers and Red Onion
summary: Succulent beef sirloin, charred peppers and red onion are threaded onto skewers and grilled hot and fast, finished with a squeeze of lemon and warm pitta. A straightforward Mediterranean-style barbecue classic that's ready in well under an hour.
equipment: barbecue or ridged cast-iron griddle pan
4 long metal skewers (or wooden skewers soaked 30 min)

ingredients.item: beef sirloin (or rump), trimmed, cut into 3.5 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
red pepper, cut into 3 cm squares
yellow pepper, cut into 3 cm squares
large red onion, cut into 8 wedges through the root, layers separated in pairs
pitta breads or flatbreads, to serve
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Stir the olive oil, garlic, lemon zest and juice, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper together in a large bowl. Add the beef and toss until every cube is coated, then cover and refrigerate for 1-4 hours. The salt seasons the meat right through, but much beyond 4 hours the lemon juice starts to turn the surface mushy.

steps.title: Prepare and thread the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the pepper squares and onion wedges with the vegetable oil. Thread beef, pepper and onion alternately onto the four skewers, leaving each piece just touching its neighbour rather than squeezed tight. Packed too tightly, the pieces in the centre of each skewer cook more slowly and unevenly than those at the ends.

steps.title: Heat the grill
steps.text: Heat the barbecue or griddle pan over high heat until very hot, roughly 10 minutes. A properly hot surface is what gives the beef and vegetables a good char rather than a grey, stewed look.

steps.title: Grill the skewers
steps.text: Grill the skewers for 8-10 minutes, giving them a quarter turn every 2 minutes so all sides get direct heat. Look for deep browning on the beef and charred edges on the peppers and onion, and check with a probe thermometer that the centre of the thickest beef cube reads 63°C. That dry, high heat sears the surface into a crust while the inside finishes cooking through.

steps.title: Rest the beef
steps.text: Lift the skewers onto a plate and cover loosely with foil for 3 minutes before serving. Resting lets the juices driven to the centre during grilling settle back through the meat, so it stays at temperature and carves more cleanly.

steps.title: Warm the pittas and serve
steps.text: Warm the pittas on the grill for 30 seconds a side, just until they puff slightly and pick up a few light marks. Serve them alongside the beef and vegetable skewers with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Cut the beef into even 3.5 cm cubes so every piece reaches 63°C at the same time; uneven sizes mean some overcook while others lag behind.
Don't marinate much longer than 4 hours — the lemon juice will start to soften and dull the texture of the meat's surface.
Leave a little space between pieces on the skewer rather than packing them tightly, so heat reaches all sides and the centres cook evenly.
Preheat the grill or griddle properly (about 10 minutes on high); this is what gives a good char without the meat stewing in its own moisture.
Always check the centre of the thickest beef cube with a probe thermometer rather than judging doneness by colour alone.
storage: Cool leftovers quickly and keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until piping hot all the way through (74°C) before eating; this dish isn't suitable for freezing once cooked, as the vegetables turn watery and soft. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
